A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Att-Adapter research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: V1 reports original FFHQ and EVOX experiments, baseline comparisons in Tables 2–4, CVAE ablations, and additional quantitative and qualitative appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds correlated-attribute examples, resource measurements, and a dropout comparison in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The decoupled cross-attention architecture, CVAE components, training objectives, and sampling procedure in Section 3 remain unchanged. Dropout is introduced as an experimental comparator, not as a component of the proposed method.

E1.justification: The face and car attribute-control coverage is retained. The full-FFHQ head-pose experiment already appears in v1 Appendix E.1 and becomes v3 Appendix F.5. The new analyses examine existing facial attributes and model configurations without adding datasets or distinct task requirements.

E2.justification: V3 Appendix F.4 adds a dropout-regularized naive adapter to the comparison with the existing naive and CVAE variants. The comparator sets in the main benchmark tables are unchanged; newly discussed ControlNet and T2I-Adapter are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The new scalability experiment varies attribute count with batch size 16 and latent dimension 1024. The new regularization comparison reports a best dropout rate of 0.25. These introduce additional experimental settings; the original numerical benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices F.1, F.3, and F.4 add focused checks of correlated-attribute disentanglement, resource scaling, and dropout versus CVAE regularization. Existing ablations and head-pose analyses are retained. F.2 discusses annotation requirements but does not add an annotation-quality experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training-run counts, seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3's added analyses provide point estimates and qualitative examples without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–9 retain their numerical results. Appendix F.4 adds 23.6% identity similarity for dropout, alongside the previously reported 28.5% naive and 6.2% CVAE values. F.3 newly reports 23,704 MB VRAM and 97 MB storage for one attribute, with increments of approximately 338 MB and 0.004 MB per additional attribute. Figure 15 adds correlated-attribute control examples.

T1.justification: The reverse-diffusion formulation, attention equation, Gaussian assumptions, CVAE ELBO, and training objective in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. The added appendix material introduces no new mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the claims of unpaired multi-attribute control, precise continuous manipulation, CVAE regularization, and superior control performance. The new appendix evidence supports these existing claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix F.2 explicitly clarifies dependence on attribute annotations and the difficulty of adapting to unannotated paired-data settings where ConceptSlider can operate. F.4 adds the interpretation that CVAE regularizes more effectively than dropout, while F.3 interprets resource measurements as supporting scalability. The existing roll-control limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V3 adds a project-page address in the abstract and documents the batch size, latent dimension, resource costs, and selected dropout rate for the new analyses. Existing implementation disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish what code or data the project page provides.

R1.justification: New Appendix B adds ControlNet and T2I-Adapter citations and expands discussion of IP-Adapter, distinguishing reference-image or spatial conditioning from numeric attribute control. Appendix F.2 also qualifies the comparison with ConceptSlider by acknowledging its applicability without explicit attribute annotations.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely verbatim. V3 adds acknowledgments, inserts Additional Related Works as Appendix B, shifts the former appendices B–E to C–F, and expands the additional-analysis subsection structure. Other wording and cross-reference edits are limited.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figure 15 and an unnumbered dropout comparison table. Existing head-pose figures are retained as Figures 16–17, with appendix figures and tables reflowed. Figure 7 replaces the named-brand prompt label with '[Italian sports]' and adds a caption explanation while retaining the same images.

improvement.justification: V1's CVAE evidence chiefly contrasts it with the naive adapter; v3 adds a dropout comparator, resource measurements, and correlated-attribute examples in Appendix F. These provide useful additional support, while the explicit annotation-dependence discussion clarifies applicability. The gains are limited: the main results remain unchanged, and the new analyses are brief, with incomplete protocol detail and no uncertainty estimates.
